title: 36-Year-Old Tennis Star Wins Every Single Game!
summary: Imagine winning a tennis match without losing a single game. That's exactly what Sorana Cirstea did at the French Open! She beat Solana Sierra 6-0, 6-0. In tennis, that's called a "double bagel" because zero looks like a bagel. And get this: Cirstea is 36 years old! She's the oldest player in the Open era to score a double bagel in a Grand Slam main draw. That's a huge deal. Cirstea has been playing professional tennis for 20 years, and she says she'll retire at the end of 2026. But right now, she's playing some of the best tennis of her life. Earlier this month, she even beat the world number one, Aryna Sabalenka! In this match, her 21-year-old opponent never even got close to winning a game. Cirstea was just too strong. She says she still works with the same discipline and always finds things to improve. "That keeps me alive," she said. Now she's into the fourth round—the farthest she's gone in a Grand Slam since 2022. If she wins her next match, she'll reach the quarterfinals at Roland Garros for the first time in 17 years! That would tie her best-ever Grand Slam result. Cirstea says what's different this season is her consistency. She's been around the top 20 for years, but now she's stringing together wins like never before. It just shows: in sports, age is just a number. Sometimes, the best moments come when you least expect them.
why_it_matters: Cirstea's win is a reminder that age does not limit you—practicing hard and believing in yourself can lead to amazing surprises, in sports or in school.

background_read: Sorana Cirstea is a professional tennis player from Romania who turned pro at age 16 and has been on the tour for two decades.
The French Open, held at Roland Garros, is one of the four Grand Slam tournaments (along with Wimbledon, the US Open, and the Australian Open) and is played on red clay courts.
Aryna Sabalenka (the world number one from Belarus) is known for her powerful strokes, so beating her is a very big deal for anyone.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sorana Cirstea, a 36-year-old Romanian tennis player in her 20th season.
WHAT: She won a French Open match 6-0, 6-0—a perfect score without losing a single game.
WHERE: At Roland Garros stadium during the French Open in Paris.
WHY: Her hard work, discipline, and new consistency helped her play some of the best tennis of her life.

perspectives.description: Older athletes like Cirstea show that peak performance can come late; her win gives hope to anyone who thinks they are past their best.
Some might say a double bagel on the big stage is even more special because the opponent never got a chance—it shows total control.
The match shows that in tennis, rankings and age don't always predict the outcome—any player can have a perfect day.
